content.value_statement: Accessibility issues block users and create compliance risk. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code WCAG 2.2 checklists, patterns, and testing guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews web interfaces against WCAG 2.2 principles and conformance levels.
Identifies common issues with alt text, labels, contrast, focus, keyboard access, and ARIA usage.
Provides accessible code patterns for modals, skip links, forms, tabs, live regions, and error handling.
Guides automated checks with Lighthouse and axe accessibility tooling.
Supports manual test planning for keyboard navigation, screen readers, zoom, contrast, and reduced motion.
limitations: Does not guarantee legal compliance or replace expert accessibility review.
Cannot verify real assistive technology behavior without testing in the target application.
Requires current page, component, or workflow context to produce specific recommendations.
Automated tooling guidance can miss issues that require human judgment.

use_cases.title: Audit a Feature Before Release
use_cases.description: Review a new page or component for WCAG 2.2 issues before it ships.

use_cases.title: Design Accessible Interaction States
use_cases.description: Check focus states, target sizes, labels, and motion alternatives during design review.

use_cases.title: Build a Manual Test Checklist
use_cases.description: Create a practical plan for keyboard, screen reader, zoom, contrast, and reduced motion testing.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page for WCAG 2.2 accessibility issues. Focus on labels, alt text, contrast, focus states, and keyboard navigation.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this component for accessibility. Explain each change and cite the WCAG area it supports.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an accessibility test plan for this feature. Include automated checks, manual keyboard tests, and screen reader checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these findings and prioritize remediation by user impact, WCAG level, implementation effort, and release risk.

output_examples.input: Audit a checkout form for accessibility issues.
output: Missing labels on required fields should be fixed first because screen reader users need programmatic names.
Error messages should be associated with each field and announced when validation fails.
Keyboard focus should move to the first invalid field after submit.

output_examples.input: Make a modal dialog keyboard accessible.
output: Use a real dialog pattern with a clear accessible name.
Move focus into the dialog when it opens and return focus when it closes.
Support Escape to close and keep Tab navigation within the dialog while open.
Run automated checks for common accessibility failures.
Test the full workflow with keyboard only.
Verify focus visibility, target size, page language, labels, error handling, and reduced motion support.

best_practices: Start with semantic HTML before adding ARIA roles or custom keyboard handling.
Combine automated checks with manual keyboard and screen reader testing.
Prioritize fixes by user impact, WCAG level, and release risk.
anti_patterns: Do not remove focus outlines without providing a visible replacement.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate errors, status, or required actions.
Do not use custom interactive elements when native controls can provide the same behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill cover WCAG 2.2?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes WCAG 2.2 criteria, conformance levels, and new requirements such as target size and focus visibility.

faq.question: Can it replace an accessibility specialist?
faq.answer: No. It helps with audits and fixes, but expert review is still important for legal and user-impact decisions.

faq.question: Does it support automated testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Lighthouse and axe checks, plus manual testing tasks that automation cannot cover.

faq.question: Can it help with screen reader support?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains labels, live regions, focus behavior, and common screen reader testing considerations.

faq.question: What kinds of interfaces does it help with?
faq.answer: It helps with web pages, forms, modals, navigation, tabs, media, notifications, and other browser-based UI patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready fixes?
faq.answer: It can suggest practical fixes, but teams should test them in the real application and assistive technology stack.
